title: The modern pantry is being rewritten around moments
summary: People don't think in categories. They think in needs, routines and moments. Jane Wakely explains why that shift is creating one of the biggest opportunities in food and beverage today.
body_markdown:
This is precisely where the opportunity lies. At PepsiCo, transformation starts with people. As the boundaries between meals and snacks continue to blur, people are eating and drinking in more places, at more times and in more ways throughout the day. New behaviors create new occasions, and new occasions give us an opportunity to create better solutions around them.


That means evolving the foods and beverages people already love while offering more choice. It means thinking beyond traditional definitions of categories and considering the full range of consumer preferences and occasions we can serve. Too often, organizations define themselves by the products they sell. The best organizations define themselves by the needs they serve.


So, my advice to leaders in our industry is simple: Don’t start with the category. Start with the consumer. Start with empathy. Start with a deep understanding of how people are actually living, working, eating and drinking, and then build around them.


The future of food and beverage will be shaped by the preferences, behaviors and occasions we are bold enough to anticipate next.


The opportunity is to stay close to consumers, understand where they’re going and evolve with them. The companies that do that best will create more choice, unlock new occasions and build brands that earn a meaningful role in people’s lives, wherever and whenever they need them.


1


According to a PepsiCo Foods survey of 1,000 nationally representative U.S. adults, conducted online by RepData from Jan. 5-21, 2026. The margin of error is plus or minus 3 percentage points.
